Thirteen shared Go/Rust cases cover ordered text/reasoning/data merges, image replacement, web query accumulation, recursive code payloads, MCP and approval codecs. Malformed known payloads fail. Nil vectors are intentionally stricter.
Preserves scope, continuation, raw object identity and timestamp policy. Raw objects never serialize. Allocated empty Go property maps normalize to Rust empty maps and emit no extra update.

Left-to-right patches retain omitted fields and support explicit false, zero, empty and clearing. Auto/none/required/named modes validate tool registration. Conservative capabilities reject unsupported modalities and duplicate tools before dispatch.
Rust domain IDs reject blank/control strings on construction and decoding. Wire message IDs remain strings to retain empty-ID folding semantics; this is an intentional API adaptation.
Baseline closed-object/required/default/keyword transformation on cloned JSON. Rust adds a depth limit and no transform cache. Go TestStrict selection passed; no live-provider dialect claim.

Explicit stable schema/version registration restores queued messages and pending requests in a fresh process; repeated restore is independent. Rejects wrong schema/type/corrupt payload. Workflow execution and graph compatibility remain P5.

Owned task group cooperatively cancels, joins before deadline, aborts and reaps timeout work; dropping shutdown aborts owned handles without cancelling parent. Adapter integration remains later phase.
